MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L31·N2036unmasked layer
This neuron fires on ordinary content/function words (mostly verbs like "have", "be", "makes", "consumed", or nouns like "lunch") in the middle of flowing conversational/narrative prose, and is strongly *suppressed* on punctuation or space tokens that sit immediately before a numeral in numeric/statistical listings (prices, NAVs, view counts, dates) — i.e. it tracks "next token is prose word" vs. "next token is a digit".

This neuron's positive side fires weakly and diffusely on clause/sentence-closing tokens in short informal blurbs — especially the final period of a sentence and the last word before a break (" page", " by", " now", " MODE") — while it is strongly *suppressed* (large negative) by mid-sentence function/verb words in fluent explanatory prose ("reduction", "made", "can", "Made").

L31·N6734unmasked layer
This neuron fires weakly-but-broadly at clause/segment boundaries and generic filler tokens (commas, sentence-final ".\n", quote+newline, " which", " one", a bare number), while being strongly *suppressed* on tokens that merely complete a predictable multi-token word or fixed collocation (e.g. "aked" in "#bakedbeans", "kers" in "retirebrokers", " vice" before "versa", " Ken" in "Kenso") — i.e. it tracks boundary/unpredictable positions vs. word-internal continuations.

L31·N12222unmasked layer
Fires mid-sentence on short grammatical "linker" tokens that open a required continuation (relative pronoun, preposition, article, degree adverb) — e.g. "characters **who** work…", "access **for** easy…", "status **as a** voucher holder", "is **often** necessary", "or **in** tetraplegic" — i.e. positions where the syntax strongly constrains what comes next; it is suppressed at clause-initial adverbs ("since", "Successfully") and list-separating commas.

This appears to be a register/context detector rather than a lexical one: it fires broadly on ordinary connective function words and punctuation (" be", " and", " a", ",", ":", "!") in the middle of casual, enthusiastic first-/second-person blog or marketing copy (website design, personal growth, sharing memories, "so cool!" link lists), while being strongly suppressed on the same kinds of tokens (" and", " is", " would") inside formal third-person expository/theological-historical prose.
